_note: Hand-written. Everything else in wild_sweep.json is machine-generated by scripts/wild_sweep.py; this file is the human triage of what it found, kept separate so the two can never be confused. Every verdict names a command that establishes it without Assay in the loop.
verified_by: uv run --extra adapters --extra sweep pytest tests/test_wild_findings.py -q

findings.claim: paws scores with includes(), a case-insensitive substring test, against the targets 'Yes' and 'No'. Any completion containing the substring is marked correct, so refusals are credited on the No class and a single constant string containing both labels is correct on every item.
findings.assay_evidence: 14 of 25 sampled items report REWARD_HACKABLE with exploit_policy=trivial:always_escalate, reported_score=1.0, true_completion=0.0, exploit_gap=1.0; task verdict INVALID. Reproducible: two full runs at --seed 0 produce byte-identical per-task results including which sample ids carry findings.

independent_verification.how: inspect_evals' own record_to_sample fixes the target vocabulary; inspect_ai's own includes() does the scoring; Assay is not in the loop

exhibits.full-dataset result: the constant completion 'yesno' scores 8000/8000 = 100.0% on paws(shuffle=False)
exhibits.not everything passes: 'Yes' is still INCORRECT for target 'No'; the scorer is loose, not broken

findings.what_assay_missed: The 100% constant-string exploit. The scripted Challenger's repertoire is the adapter's trivial policies and none of them names both labels at once, so it found the refusal exploit and hand triage found the stronger one. TRIVIAL_FLOOR_BREACH also did not fire, correctly: the escalate policy averages 0.56 over the sample against gold's 1.0, and the probe's rule is that a trivial policy must tie or beat the best real one.

findings.reported_by: hand triage during paws follow-up; assay reported boolq clean
findings.claim: boolq scores with pattern(r'(Yes|No).?\Z'). Anchoring at the end of the completion is a real mitigation, but '.?' admits one trailing character and 'know' is 'no' plus 'w', so a bare 'I don't know' is scored CORRECT on every No-targeted item.
findings.assay_evidence: none - assay reported 0 findings on boolq, with 8 probes run and passed

independent_verification.how: inspect_ai's own pattern() scorer, with the regex read from inspect_evals' boolq.py

exhibits.no constant string satisfies both target: 'yesno' is CORRECT for 'No' and INCORRECT for 'Yes'

independent_verification.scope_of_the_leak: closes with any trailing punctuation; two trailing characters do not match

findings.why_assay_missed_it: The scripted Challenger's trivial vocabulary is a fixed set of strings, so whether it finds a substring leak depends on which string it happens to hold. Its refusal ends in 'answer.', which does not match the anchored pattern. This is the argument for the prompted Challenger.

observations.subject: unseeded dataset shuffle
observations.verdict: CONFIRMED for paws by execution; SURVEY only for the rest
observations.claim: paws and boolq default to shuffle=True with no seed, so any run using --limit N draws different items each time and two limited runs are not comparable.
observations.independent_verification: two identical paws() calls returned sample ids ['7531','6916','818',...] and ['7622','1046','5001',...]; paws(shuffle=False) returned ['1','2','3',...] both times
observations.survey: 35 task modules under inspect_evals/ default to unseeded shuffle; sad and assistant_bench are the ones that pass a seed. The survey is a source survey and is not claimed as verified per task.
observations.why_assay_missed_it: The determinism probe checks that scoring is reproducible given a fixed dataset, not that dataset construction is. A genuine gap in the family, recorded rather than quietly patched into a probe this workstream did not scope.

zero_finding_claim: Every other swept task reported no defect. That statement is only readable because probes_passed names which probes ran: a task showing eight probes run and passed is a different result from one where every probe reported NOT_APPLICABLE, and the two are indistinguishable from a finding count alone.
